## New Cross-Domain Connection

- **[2026-11-06] Fred's Terrain Autobattler already has a working savings rule: +1 gold for every 10 held, up to +3. His Children's Financial Literacy Game stub has had "teach saving and compound interest" as its whole design since May, with no mechanic. The first game already holds a tested mechanic for the second.** [[games/terrain-autobattler-factions-units-economy]] sets income at 5 gold base per round, +1 for each 10 held (max +3) and +1 per PvP win, with no streak gold. Its AI opponents run `greedy`, `balanced` or `aggressive` economy styles. `raw/games/Childrens Financial Literacy Game.md` (listed in [[games/prototypes]]) says the game should teach "saving, spending, earning, compound interest", and its Lightfin todo (coral coins) has been open since 05-01. Two points make the borrowing worth doing, not just noting. (1) The autobattler's interest does compound, because interest gold counts toward the next round's holdings. But the +3 cap means saving past 30 gold earns nothing extra, so the best play is "save up to a target, then spend the surplus". That is a sound budgeting lesson for kids, but it is not how real compound interest works. If the kids' game copies the mechanic, it must decide on purpose whether to keep the cap (budget lesson) or remove it (growth lesson). (2) The game's existing 2,000-fight balance harness ([[games/terrain-autobattler-map-pipeline]], used today for map fairness) runs single fights on fixed boards, not whole matches, so it does not yet test economy. Extended to full AI-vs-AI matches, it could answer with numbers the question a kids' game would try to teach: how often the `greedy` economy beats the `aggressive` one. Smallest next step: when [[games/prototypes]] is filled in, have the financial-literacy row cite the autobattler's income table as its starting mechanic, and record the cap decision there.

## New Cross-Domain Connection

- **[2026-11-05] Today's podcast pick, *The Doctor's Kitchen*, gives the recipe recommender the health-led chef it has never had. The host is a GP who cooks, and the episode the pick suggests starting with is Tommy Wood, the author of Health's main dementia source.** [[podcasts/suggestions]] (week of 2026-11-05) recommends Dr Rupy Aujla's show. Its suggested first episode is Wood's "7 habits a neuroscientist swears by" (Mar 2026). Wood also wrote the Ferriss guest post behind [[health/source-wood-brain-sharp-2026]], but the pick never says so and frames the show as a follow-on to the Candow creatine episode instead. The Cooking side is the gap: the recipe recommender says it is "inspired by Fred's chef profiles", and [[cooking/chefs]] lists only four, Quinn, Slater, Bourdain and Chang. None of them cooks to a health target, which fits the 10-09 idea's finding that only two of the first 42 suggestions were oily-fish mains. Aujla publishes recipes built around exactly this kind of target (his Doctor's Kitchen cookbooks; general knowledge, not from a wiki source). **Why it matters:** a fifth chef page for Aujla in [[cooking/chefs]] is the smallest change that would steer the Friday batch toward Health without rewriting the recommender prompt or waiting for [[health/my-protocol]]'s Diet section to be filled in. Listening to the Wood episode first would also show whether his advice has changed since the April source page, which is still the wiki's only dementia-diet reference.

- Nothing fully resolved: the 11-04 briefing withdrew the ORCL put close, but the drop's cause and a written exit rule are still missing.
